title: libgraph double-buffer layout and DISPLAY in VCK units (MAGH/DW)
problem: (1) Upstream sceGsSetDefDBuffDc uses fbp1 = zbufAddr (GS.cpp:906), so the second framebuffer lands on the Z buffer. (2) Every sceGsSetDefDispEnv / DBuff / DBuffDc / ResetGraph stub builds DISPLAY with MAGH=0 and DW=w-1. Hardware reads DW in video clocks.
approach: fbp1 = fbw*ceil(h/pageLines), where pageLines is 64 for 16-bit PSM and 32 otherwise. New makeLibgraphDisplay(dx,dy,w,h): MAGH = min(ceil(2560/w)-1, 15), DW = (MAGH+1)*w-1. The upstream CPU backend computes (DW+1)/(MAGH+1), so its output does not change.
scope_evidence: general (every libgraph game; matters for any accurate GS backend)
reference: PCSX2 pcsx2/GS/GSState.cpp ~7326: magnification = MAGH+1, renderWidth = (DW+1)/magnification, final width capped at DW/(VideoModeDivider+1). With upstream MAGH=0, DW=639 the real-GS width would be 160 px.
upstream_equivalent: #336 (lay out sceGsSetDefDBuff/DispEnv/zbufaddr like libgraph), #186, #331; srwz-03 is a superset

title: EE FPU: SQRT.S reads ft; CVT.W.S truncates and saturates
problem: Upstream fpu_translator.cpp:61 emits FPU_SQRT_S(ctx->f[fs]); on the EE the operand is in the ft field. FPU_CVT_W_S uses nearbyintf (round to nearest).
approach: SQRT.S uses the ft field, sqrt(|ft|), sign-preserved zero, I/SI flags on negative input. CVT.W.S truncates when exponent <= 0x4E800000, else 0x7FFFFFFF / 0x80000000 by sign. The fork's DIV.S/RSQRT.S changes are already covered upstream by #272 (ps2_fdiv/ps2_frsqrt).
reference: PCSX2 pcsx2/FPU.cpp: SQRT_S uses _FtValUl_ and sqrt(fabs(ft)); CVT_W: (s32) cast when (Fs & 0x7F800000) <= 0x4E800000, else 0x7fffffff / 0x80000000. Verified.

title: EE EABI varargs for printf-family stubs: 8 arg registers, then 8-byte stack slots from caller sp+0; va_list steps 8 bytes; %q, %h/%hh, %ld = 64-bit
problem: Upstream (Support.h:784, 802, 855) uses an o32 model: stack base sp+0x10, 4-byte slots, even-slot alignment for 64-bit values; va_list steps 4 bytes. On the EE every vararg is one 64-bit register or 8-byte slot, so printf/sprintf/vsprintf output with more than 8 args, or with doubles/long long, is garbage.
approach: readSlot reads a full 64-bit register (r[4+i]) or 8-byte slot at sp+(i-8)*8. va_list reads 8 bytes and steps 8.
reference: Fork's disassembly of SRWZ newlib vfprintf 0x1a19b0 and sceSnprintf 0x11dc90; not independently verified by me. Consistent with upstream's own comment that EE calls use a0-a3,t0-t3.
